comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. NO POLYGON: OpenStreetMap has no landuse=winter_sports polygon for Boreal (checked 2026-11-19: relation/3184061, 'Boreal Mountain Resort', is a type=site, site=piste relation that lists most of its lifts and runs, not an area), so resorts.json sets "ski_area": "derived": the area is drawn from the resort's own kept lifts and runs, buffered by 100 m (one part, 1.45 km²; the resort says 380 acres). Boreal is one face above Interstate 80 at the Castle Peak exit, its seven lifts from one base (the Base Lodge and the Woodward Tahoe Bunker) to Boreal Ridge, on one ticket and one map; no part is reached only by road or shuttle. NEIGHBOURS: no lift or trail joins Boreal to Donner Ski Ranch, Soda Springs or Sugar Bowl on any of their maps or in OpenStreetMap, so each has its own map (the owner's rule of 2026-11-14). Sugar Bowl (relation/10326057, south of Donner Pass Road, 1.1 km from Boreal's nearest run) is a listed neighbour in resorts.json (157 features left out). Donner Ski Ranch (relation/3184079) and Soda Springs (relation/3185906) have only type=site relations, no polygon, so they cannot be listed, and each of their lifts and runs in the Overpass window is hidden here one by one, as Sugar Bowl's file hides them: Donner Ski Ranch's 8 lifts (its tubing carpet among them) and 47 runs (the bottom of its Chair 5 lies 150 m from Boreal's Sunrise Blvd., the two areas' closest approach), Soda Springs' 5 lifts and 18 runs (2 km west), and the two unnamed rope tows by Soda Springs Road on no resort's relation. With a derived ski area a listed neighbour leaves out only what its polygon holds at least half of, so three Sugar Bowl features outside Sugar Bowl's polygon are hidden too (the Sugar Rush tubing carpet, an unnamed run on the Crow's Peak side and the Lincoln East Face backcountry area): otherwise they would be kept and add parts to the derived area. Quicksilver, a disused chair (OSM disused=yes, operator Boreal) south-east of the Lost Dutchman and the 49er, on neither the trail map nor the lift report, is hidden. Each neighbour's hide expects the element's kind and name only, so a rating edit at a neighbour never stops this build; a polygon mapped for Donner Ski Ranch or Soda Springs later replaces its hides with a neighbours entry, and one mapped for Boreal itself replaces "derived" with its id (a new version). Nothing of Boreal's own is lost: every lift and run its site relation lists is kept (Bonanza, the California Cruiser and the Magic Carpet, which the relation omits, are Boreal's too). WOODWARD TAHOE: the Woodward Mountain Parks are Boreal's terrain parks: OSM's Jibassic Park, Pacific Highline Park and Progression Park are snow parks and the Halfpipe a man_made=piste:halfpipe run, all four with the park flag; the indoor Bunker and the summer parks are not in OSM's piste data (no building is tagged as a run), and the Tahoe Tubing lanes (piste:type=sled) are left out by the type rule. RATINGS AND NAMES: every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-19 against the resort's 2025-26 trail map (rideboreal.com/explore/facilities/trail-maps, BIG_Boreal_96x48_TrailMap_25-26.jpg, 6912 x 3456 px, read in crops: green circle, blue square, black diamond and the orange Woodward park symbols), the trail lists on that page (Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced) and the lift and trail report (the data behind rideboreal.com/explore/status-conditions/lift-trail-status: eight winter lifts with the Tahoe Tubing Carpet, 34 alpine trails rated Easiest, More Difficult or Most Difficult and 10 terrain parks). The three agree on every run they share, and every named OSM run carries their rating but one: Undertow, a blue square on the map, intermediate on the page and more difficult in the report, novice in OSM (an old TIGER road), becomes intermediate. OSM's novice Sunrise Blvd. and Sunset Blvd. are green on the map (both draw green). Names: the chair OSM calls Flying Dutchman, its old name, becomes the Lost Dutchman (the report's Lost Dutchman Triple Chairlift and the page's 'gullies on the Lost Dutchman'; the map labels it DUTCHMAN), and Kangroo Cornice becomes Kangaroo Cornice (the map, the page and the report). Names that differ from the map only by punctuation or a suffix stay as OSM has them (Sunrise Blvd. and Sunset Blvd. for SUNRISE BLVD and SUNSET BLVD, the Accelerator for ACCELERATOR QUAD); the map's MAGIC CARPET is OSM's Magic Carpet (the report's Discovery Carpet). OSM GAPS (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): 8 of the resort's 34 runs are not in OpenStreetMap: Murphy's Way and Adventure Trail (green), Sierra (blue), Tamarack, Klondike, Mogul Rock, Blizzard Ridge and Westward Ho (black); nor are the map's Sierra Park, Big Blue Park, Peace Park, Woodward Start Park and Family Fun Cross.

overrides.reason: The resort's lift report names this chair the Lost Dutchman Triple Chairlift, its trail-map page sends riders to 'the gullies on the Lost Dutchman', and its 2025-26 trail map labels it DUTCHMAN; OSM's Flying Dutchman is the chair's old name.
Misspelling: the resort's 2025-26 trail map, its trail-map page and its lift and trail report all spell the run Kangaroo Cornice (OSM Kangroo Cornice).

Undertow is a blue square (more difficult) on the resort's 2025-26 trail map, intermediate on its trail-map page and more difficult in its lift and trail report; OSM rates it novice (the way is an old road from the TIGER import). The resort's sources agree and win.
